key_insight: Nano- and micro-textures improve perovskite solar cells not only by trapping light, but also by enhancing wetting, crystallinity, charge extraction, and mechanical robustness.
engineering_relevance: For device engineers, textured interfaces offer a multi-functional design strategy to raise efficiency and durability in perovskite photovoltaics, photodetectors, and LEDs.
method: Review of recently reported texture-related benefits beyond optical management
Focus on effects on perovskite film formation, crystal quality, and carrier extraction
Considers mechanical effects for flexible devices, including bending stability and residual stress
evidence_signal: The paper synthesizes recent reported results showing texture-related gains in wetting, grain size/orientation, phase homogeneity, open-circuit voltage, and mechanical stability.
watch_item: Benefits are reported across different texture types and device stacks, so performance gains may depend strongly on fabrication compatibility and process control.
paper_title: More than just light management -- The multiple advantages of nano- and micro-textures in perovskite solar cells
